blocks.text: How can we compare two algorithms without running them? Asymptotic notation provides a way to describe their performance as input size grows.

blocks.markdown: Asymptotic notation is a mathematical tool used to describe the behavior of functions as their input size approaches infinity. It allows us to compare the efficiency of algorithms by focusing on their growth rates rather than specific execution times.

blocks.title: Big-O Notation
blocks.text: Big-O notation, denoted as $O(f(n))$, describes an upper bound on the growth rate of a function. It provides a way to express the worst-case scenario of an algorithm's time or space complexity.

blocks.latex: f(n) = O(g(n)) \text{ if there exist constants } c > 0 \text{ and } n_0 \text{ such that } f(n) \leq c \cdot g(n) \text{ for all } n \geq n_0.
blocks.caption: Formal definition of Big-O notation.

blocks.title: Applying Big-O Notation
blocks.prompt: Determine the Big-O notation for the function $f(n) = 3n^2 + 2n + 1$.

steps.text: Identify the term that grows the fastest as $n$ increases. Here, $3n^2$ is the dominant term.
Express $f(n)$ in terms of Big-O notation by ignoring lower-order terms and constant factors. Thus, $f(n) = O(n^2)$.

blocks.markdown: Big-O notation simplifies the analysis by focusing on the most significant term, which dominates the function's growth as $n$ becomes large. This abstraction helps compare algorithms based on their efficiency.

blocks.title: Omega Notation
blocks.text: Omega notation, denoted as $\Omega(f(n))$, provides a lower bound on the growth rate of a function. It describes the best-case scenario or minimum performance of an algorithm.

blocks.title: Theta Notation
blocks.text: Theta notation, denoted as $\Theta(f(n))$, describes a tight bound on the growth rate of a function. It indicates that a function grows at the same rate as $f(n)$, both in the upper and lower bounds.

blocks.title: Comparing Growth Rates
blocks.prompt: Rank the following functions by their growth rates: $f(n) = n \log n$, $g(n) = n^2$, $h(n) = 2^n$.

steps.text: Identify the growth rate of each function: $f(n) = n \log n$, $g(n) = n^2$, $h(n) = 2^n$.
Compare their growth rates: $n \log n < n^2 < 2^n$.

blocks.markdown: The constant factors and lower-order terms are omitted in asymptotic notation because they become insignificant as $n$ grows large. However, in practice, these factors can matter for small input sizes or when comparing algorithms with similar growth rates.

blocks.title: Practical Considerations
blocks.text: While asymptotic notation provides a high-level comparison, the actual performance can vary based on constant factors, lower-order terms, and real-world constraints like memory usage and I/O operations.

points: Big-O, Omega, and Theta notations describe upper, lower, and tight bounds on function growth rates.
Asymptotic notation focuses on dominant terms, ignoring constant factors and lower-order terms.
Practical performance can differ due to real-world constraints and smaller input sizes.
